evidence: Hor. C. 2.16.13–14: splendet in mēnsā tenuī salīnum
terms.comment: Latin does not tell “on” from “in”: in mēnsā, on the table; in pariete, on the wall; in terrā, on earth. For “on top of”, super (see on top of).

evidence: Cic. Sen. 34: in equum omnīnō nōn ascendere
terms.comment: Of motion onto a thing: in equum ascendere, get on a horse; in mēnsam, onto the table.

evidence: Mor. 81: vēnālēs umerō fascēs portābat in urbem
terms.comment: With verbs of carrying and riding the ablative often stands alone: equō vehī, ride on a horse; umerō portāre, carry on one’s shoulder.

phrases.latin: vīvitur parvō bene, cui paternum splendet in mēnsā tenuī salīnum
phrases.english: he lives well on little whose father’s salt-cellar shines on a plain table

phrases.latin: canis ingēns, catēnā vīnctus, in pariete erat pictus
phrases.english: a huge dog on a chain was painted on the wall

phrases.latin: Glōria in altissimīs Deō, et in terrā pāx hominibus bonae voluntātis.
phrases.english: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.

phrases.latin: cum ingressus iter pedibus sit, in equum omnīnō nōn ascendere; cum autem equō, ex equō nōn dēscendere
phrases.english: when he has set out on foot, he will not get on a horse at all; but when on horseback, he will not get off

phrases.latin: vēnālēs umerō fascēs portābat in urbem
phrases.english: he used to carry bundles for sale on his shoulder into town
